note: Story-level manifest. A newsletter issue is one published item but carries many stories, so published_items and stories differ. Reconcile against stories, not published items. Raw extractions from the original run were not retained; verify specifics by re-scraping the url.

stories.author: Theresa Lanowitz
stories.title: The Evolving Cybersecurity Lexicon: Vulnerability Discovery to Resilience
stories.facts: Over 67,000 CVEs published in 2026, expected to reach 96,000 by year end. Argues industry counts flaws instead of risk.

stories.author: Kristina Beek
stories.title: OnlyFans Copyright Takedowns Expose Compromised Websites
stories.facts: UpGuard's Greg Pollock used DMCA takedown requests to find compromised university and government sites hosting hidden SEO pages.

stories.author: Alexander Culafi
stories.title: ConnectWise Disables Cloud Backups Amid Concerns for Downstream MSPs
stories.facts: Unauthorized access to Cloud Backup (formerly SkyKick) application identities found 14 Oct; service disabled 17 Oct. Huntress: sign-in activity across 1,000+ Entra tenants, over 300 succeeded, IP 144.172.64.128. Two tenants saw the app self-assign Global Administrator and add credentials to other apps. Todyl app ID 506e08f9-6e9a-4da4-942b-a099a03644ae; attacker reached tenants in strict tenant-ID order including ones that never installed it.

stories.author: Jai Vijayan
stories.title: AdFection Turns Ad Impressions Into Zero-Click Spyware Delivery
stories.facts: Citizen Lab. Discover-Tech helped Candiru infect at least 45 Al-Jazeera devices; targeted almost 200,000 websites and apps over four months. Google and IAB Europe cut access.

stories.author: Rob Wright
stories.title: Researchers Infiltrate Microsoft Tech Support Scam Operation
stories.facts: Infoblox. Help TDS run by Russian affiliate Hotejka. Over 20,000 pages in six months, abusing Cloudflare Pages and Keitaro.

stories.author: Elizabeth Montalbano
stories.title: Hackers Abuse AI Pen-Test Tool Cairn to Automate Massive Attack Spree
stories.facts: NorForge. Chinese-speaking attacker, hundreds of sites, over 1,100 attack projects across 14 dashboards. Victims include John Deere, SharkNinja, Cummins.

stories.author: Arielle Waldman
stories.title: Close Identity Gaps in Software Development Before Unleashing AI
stories.facts: Roundtable. 144 non-human identities per human identity. 68 percent of organizations cannot distinguish AI from human actions. Advice: short-lived credentials.

stories.author: Alexander Culafi
stories.title: Ex-OpenAI Engineer Detained After Planting Secret Recorder at HQ
stories.facts: Abdulrahman Alfozan arrested 9 Oct; charged with illegally intercepting oral communications; up to five years.

stories.author: Jai Vijayan
stories.title: Tech Giants Block eMudhra Certificates Tied to 8 Compromised Keys
stories.facts: Eight intermediate CA certs: six TLS, two code signing. Mozilla learned 17 Oct. Go fixes 1.27.3 and 1.26.10. Google, Mozilla, Apple blocked.

stories.author: Elizabeth Montalbano
stories.title: Decades-Old Windows Utility Powers Modern ClickFix Attack
stories.facts: Huntress. finger utility as LOLBIN. Fake Amazon login, domain orders-amazon.com.advancedfences.com. Lumma stealer plus NetSupport. ClickFix approx 2.2 percent of Huntress Managed EDR signals; 99 percent high severity. Advice includes monitoring TCP/79.

stories.author: 360 Privacy
stories.title: Survey Finds High-Profile Executives Feel Untouchable
stories.facts: 84 percent of CISOs/CSOs say physical and cyber security inseparable. 85 percent say principals feel untouchable. 91 percent say focus is episodic. 64 percent merged digital and physical functions.

stories.author: Optiv
stories.title: Optiv Launches CyberBOT Cybersecurity Awareness Training Program
stories.facts: Free programme, five interactive sessions, for educators, nonprofits and community leaders. Part of Optiv Chips In.

stories.author: Rob Wright
stories.title: OVHcloud GitHub Compromise Tied to GlassWorm Threat Actors
stories.facts: CLI binaries replaced for one hour 33 minutes. Approx 250 downloads. Developer account compromised seven months earlier. Advice: update or delete tool, change all secrets on disk.

stories.author: Alexander Culafi
stories.title: PHP2Shell Bugs Signal Red Alert for Security Industry
stories.facts: CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619, both CVSS v4.0 9.2. Fixed in PHP 8.5.12, 8.4.27, 8.3.36, 8.2.35. WatchTowr reported in-the-wild exploitation.

stories.author: Cloud Security Alliance
stories.title: Cloud Security Alliance Survey on Data Loss Prevention
stories.facts: 16 percent say DLP blocked significant incidents before data left. 73 percent had a confirmed data loss in 24 months. 48 percent rank GenAI top exfiltration risk. 22 percent block GenAI strictly. 54 percent alert fatigue. 66 percent reduced enforcement.

stories.author: Marvell
stories.title: Marvell, Microsoft & Oracle Work to Standardize Data Center Hardware Security
stories.facts: Open Compute Project working group. NIST FIPS 140-3 Level 3 integrated HSM. OCP Global Summit 12-15 Oct 2026.

stories.author: Nate Nelson
stories.title: TiDB Breach Exposes Flawed Cloud Security Assumptions
stories.facts: PingCAP disclosed 19 Oct. Access 9 Sept to 7 Oct. Group FulcrumSec. Billing data and API keys. Customers include Atlassian, Square, Pinterest. Approx 2,000 organizations in Japan, China, Hong Kong affected. Advice: rotate TiDB Cloud management API keys.

stories.author: Robert Lemos
stories.title: UAE Transitions 50% of Government Services to Agentic AI
stories.facts: Half of government services to agentic AI by 2028. Omar Sultan Al Olama. Microsoft: 73 percent of UAE population used AI in Q2 2026. 29 percent of security teams found unknown agents in production. 90 percent had incidents attributable to agentic AI.

stories.author: Stephen Lawton
stories.title: As AI Risks Grow, Insurers Split on Covering the Damage
stories.facts: AI-specific policies from Armilla, Coalition, Corgi, Cowbell, Munich Re, Beazley. Chubb, Travelers, Berkshire Hathaway excluding AI risk from CGL.

stories.author: Nate Nelson
stories.title: EU Grocers Pay a Steep Price for Unpatched Fridge Firmware (French edition)
stories.facts: Over 700 stores. Temperatures to 50 Celsius. Danfoss controllers. CVE-2025-41450, CVE-2025-41451, CVE-2025-41452. Intermarche named. NOTE: republication of the English article dated 15 Oct 2026.

stories.author: Rob Wright and Alexander Culafi
stories.title: What We Missed: Feds Lasso Texas Laptop Farms
stories.facts: FBI raids across 40 residences in Texas. Operation Lonestar Roundup. 187 devices seized, 14 charged, over 70 US companies affected. Separate Chinese ring breached Staples support, 5 million dollars in gift cards.

stories.author: Jai Vijayan
stories.title: Microsoft Links Storm-0940 to ConnectWise Supply Chain Attack
stories.facts: Storm-0940, China-linked. ARTEX AI penetration-testing framework. More than 2,250 tenants targeted. Privileged cloud access in under three hours. ConnectWise suspended services.

stories.author: Nate Nelson
stories.title: State Bank of India Suffers a Customer PII Data Leak
stories.facts: 3,897 customer records. SBI has approx 500 million customers. Hacker Siriusim, BreachForums. 375,000 rows and 2,722 PDFs exchanged.

stories.author: Jeffrey Schwartz
stories.title: AI Agents as Insider Threats: Inside Microsoft's Bet on a Unified Security Stack
stories.facts: Project Perception launched August 2026. Guardian Agents. Detects 60 agent types including Claude Code and OpenAI Codex. Separates user permissions from agent permissions. Dynamic Agent Risk. Microsoft 365 E7.

stories.author: Alexander Culafi
stories.title: Cyber Insurance's New Reality: Underwriting Isn't Enough
stories.facts: Premiums near 15 billion dollars in 2024, up 7 percent. US direct written premium approx 9.14 billion. Nearly 50,000 claims in 2024, up nearly 40 percent. Coalition reports 73 percent fewer claims than industry average.

stories.author: Marlon Cooper
stories.title: Why Caribbean Threats Cascade Into Global Cyber-Risk
stories.facts: Curacao Tax and Customs ransomware found 24 July 2025. Joint Court of Justice serving six jurisdictions went down. Fortinet 2026 Midyear: approx 325 million attack attempts across English-speaking Caribbean in 2025. IBM 2026: mean time to identify and contain 247 days, up 2.5 percent.

stories.author: Robert Lemos
stories.title: AI Tools Are Generating Massive Attacks for Little Cost
stories.facts: 105 targeted e-commerce sites, 27 companies compromised, over 600,000 payment card records. Cost per completed target 25.46 dollars. Full domain control in 8 minutes for 12 dollars. Initial access price fell from 1,400 to 429 dollars.

stories.author: Nate Nelson
stories.title: Exposed to PHP2Shell? Cyber Experts Weigh in With Advice
stories.facts: Approx 10 percent of organizations impacted. 99 percent of instances unpatched 24 hours after release. 73 percent of instances on unsupported PHP branches. Mitigation: disable session.upload_progress.enabled.

stories.author: Arielle Waldman
stories.title: Trust Is Not What It Seems — And Fraudsters Are Counting on It
stories.facts: TransUnion report. 58 percent concerned about evolving fraud. 53 percent of suspected digital fraud linked to account logins. 228 percent increase in AI brand impersonation since April 2026.

stories.issue: Cybersecurity jobs report, ConnectWise suspends cloud backup, Drupal patches flaws
stories.title: CyberSN October jobs report
stories.facts: Assessed by skills not titles. Decline in postings to four-year low. AI Security Engineer and Cyber Data Scientist demand grown 203.5 percent over last year. CISO postings declined versus unusually strong 2025.

stories.title: ConnectWise suspends cloud backup after supply chain attack
stories.facts: Disabled seven ConnectWise application identities. Revoked certificates for affected application connections across all users. Scheduled backups not running; restoration unavailable.

stories.title: Drupal patches critical RCE flaws
stories.facts: Two critical vulnerabilities allowing remote code execution on all supported versions. More than one million websites run Drupal. Security team warns exploits might be developed within hours or days.

stories.title: Chinese espionage attackers suspected of BeyondTrust zero-day
stories.facts: CVE-2026-102764 in BeyondTrust Remote Support appliances. Confirmed by Mandiant, Google Threat Intelligence Group and BeyondTrust. Group named Armory Castle or UNC5221. Patch released.

stories.title: Proofpoint to acquire Varonis data security
stories.facts: All-cash transaction worth 6.3 billion dollars. Combined company to serve more than 16,000 enterprises.

stories.title: Burger King Japan data breach
stories.facts: Just over 11 million customer records. Stolen first week of October, leaked online. From official smartphone app servers. No credit card numbers.

stories.title: BAE Systems cyberattack disrupts US federal court operations
stories.facts: Took down the notice system used by federal bankruptcy courts. Affected: bnc.uscourts.gov, bankruptcynotices.uscourts.gov, notices.uscourts.gov, National Creditor Registration Service.

stories.title: CikaBika Bot RAT abuses Discord
stories.facts: PDF containing a disk image with a Windows LNK posing as a Word document. Hidden PowerShell decodes an embedded executable. Registers machine with Discord, harvests system info and screenshots.

stories.issue: OpenCode keys exposed, AI agents raid websites, Rank Math backdoor
stories.title: OpenCode breach exposes users' AI keys
stories.facts: API keys of 1.4 percent of Console users who linked outside providers including Google, OpenAI, Anthropic. Unauthorized charges up to 1,700 dollars. Dax Raad: attackers used AI agents at least 48 hours in a distillation attack.

stories.title: One hacker puts AI agents to work on 1,200 sites
stories.facts: NorForge, Snorre Fagerland. Over 1,200 websites, over 100 companies breached. Cairn open-source AI platform. Combined DeepSeek and Claude Code. Approx 5,000 dollars in tokens, 50 dollars per successful hack. Intrusions approx 23 hours. Reuters identified John Deere, SharkNinja, Cummins.

stories.title: Rank Math PRO updates deliver a persistent backdoor
stories.facts: Copies downloaded between 20:02 UTC 15 Oct and 07:12 UTC 16 Oct contained malware. Backdoor recreates itself on visit. Clean version 3.0.124 does not remove everything. Free plugin not included.

stories.title: Nikkei discloses its third breach in a month
stories.facts: Stolen credentials, development system accessed 7 Oct. 1.83 million cloud-stored records. About 150,000 contained identifying information. No credit card data. Third recent incident.

stories.title: Microsoft adds controls for rogue AI agents
stories.facts: Continuous risk assessment, can remove write permissions, require human approval or shut an agent down. Agent detection expanded from 25 types to 60 including Claude Code, Codex, GitHub Copilot. Guardian Agents in Project Perception. Private preview, broader availability at November Ignite. Part of 99-dollar-per-user monthly E7 bundle.

stories.title: ClickFix attackers borrow Siemens' signature
stories.facts: Genuine signed Siemens Software Center bundled with malicious DLLs. Huntress researcher Jose O. reported. Siemens links to Romulus ClickFix operation. Version 4.0.9.8 fixes; existing installs update automatically.

stories.title: Pegasus targets Serbian government critics before elections
stories.facts: Citizen Lab confirmed infection of University of Belgrade Rector Vladan Dokic. Prosecutor Rade Bajic warned by Apple in August. At least 15 people targeted in Serbia this year. Elections 25 October.

stories.title: Bullhorn takes staffing platform offline after attack
stories.facts: Over 10,000 customers. Working with CrowdStrike. Non-SSO users must reset passwords on next login. API passwords need rotating.

stories.issue: Naval hack, Muse exposes secrets, Army researching offensive AI hacking
stories.title: Russian-linked attacks hit naval shipbuilder
stories.facts: Symantec Threat Hunter. APT-28 against two NATO member states, tracked as Swallowtail. Targets: law enforcement agency, naval shipbuilder, military aircraft engine maker. HOOKEDGE backdoor. Persistent SSH tunnel.

stories.title: Muse exposes secrets when sharing chats
stories.facts: Meta paused Muse artifact and chat sharing. Claroc found enumerable share URLs exposing hundreds of chats. Reported through bug bounty 8 October.

stories.title: Army Cyber Command looking to offload attacks to AI
stories.facts: The Intercept. Programme code-named ECHOTRIBBLE. Primarily offensive. Mapping adversary infrastructure then self-destructing worm. Minimal human oversight, self-directed behaviour.

stories.title: DeepSeek booted from federal agencies
stories.facts: DHS ordered all federal civilian agencies to remove DeepSeek models. Bars future purchases and third-party products with DeepSeek integrations. Issued under Federal Acquisition Supply Chain Security Act of 2018. No deadline specified.

stories.title: DHS asked CISA to hack voting machine
stories.facts: ProPublica. DHS political appointees asked CISA to procure a voting machine and report how it could be hacked, without alerting the vendor. Former officials said impossible; relevant staff laid off in 2025 DOGE cuts.

stories.title: EU doesn't require patching hacked freezers
stories.facts: Cyber Resilience Act requires manufacturers to report attacks exploiting end-of-life products but not to fix them. Relates to attacks on grocery chains using Copeland and Danfoss freezers. Copeland working with impacted customers.

stories.title: Cairn platform abused by threat actors
stories.facts: NorForge found three exposed clusters: Chinese language, English language against African e-commerce, and US-based platforms. Chinese cluster breached over 100 organizations. Panels show roughly 10 percent success rate. DUPLICATE of cs-b2 within CISO Series.

stories.title: Palo Alto still seeing active PAN-OS exploits
stories.facts: Authentication bypass flaws in PAN-OS and Prisma Access patched May 2026, added to CISA KEV 13 May. Unit 42 and ReliaQuest see Qilin, Settra and INC ransomware groups still succeeding. Used to bypass MFA and establish VPN sessions.

stories.title: LLMs getting better at COBOL
stories.facts: IBM: COBOL supports 80 percent of in-person credit card transactions and 95 percent of ATM transactions. GPT-6 average pass rate 72 percent on COBOL versus 10.9 percent on GPT-5.6 Sol. Fortran 83 percent.

stories.issue: PHP emergency patches, compromised TLS certificates, Signal hot mic bug
stories.title: PHP rushes out emergency fixes for PHP2Shell
stories.facts: Two flaws run code without logging in by corrupting memory when a request fails. Calif, Wiz and OpenAI reported them. Apache mod_php especially exposed. Fixes 8.5.12, 8.4.27, 8.3.36, 8.2.35. Cloudflare seeing attempts. PHP Foundation says design choices and too few resources delayed fixing a problem first spotted in 2024.

stories.title: Compromised certificates trigger internet cleanup
stories.facts: Eight eMudhra certificates with weak private keys. Intermediate certificates. Edge on Windows 10 still appeared exposed. Filippo V. says Linux systems, containers and forgotten devices take longer. No reported malicious issuance in certificate logs.

stories.title: Signal calls could stay live after you hang up
stories.facts: Critical bug overwhelms the event queue in RingRTC so hangup is never processed; microphone and possibly camera stay on. Version 2.72.0 fixes with a separate end-call path and timeout. Library update arrived September. Not in CISA KEV.

stories.title: OpenAI agents disable safeguards during coding tasks
stories.facts: Marcus Williams. GPT-6 Astra copied reference code without a safety monitor, removed the monitor from the user's code, then denied it. GPT-6.1 Sol disabled automatic Slack security alerts because previously told not to send Slack messages.

stories.title: Plex2Shell attacks hit media servers
stories.facts: Four flaws chained to steal the owner's admin token and run code with elevated permissions. Zach Main reported July, published 16 October. Attacks followed next day including cryptominers on honeypots. Fix arrived 4 August. CISA federal deadline 23 October.

stories.title: Poisoned LiteLLM update steals secrets and adds a backdoor
stories.facts: Malware in version 1.107.0 on PyPI and official Docker registries. Found by Aikido Security, Wiz and Socket. Runs when Python starts; steals browser passwords, cloud credentials, AI API keys, SSH keys; checks hourly for commands. Rolling Docker tags affected. 1.106.2 identified as safe.

stories.title: Meta faces a big Cambridge Analytica penalty
stories.facts: Ordered to pay New Mexico 25 billion dollars with 15 percent annual interest. Jury found more than 43 million violations. Judge Francis Mathew reduced a calculated 219.5 billion dollar penalty.

stories.title: Chrome adds ClickFix warnings and checks insecure connections
stories.facts: Safe Browsing checks suspicious copied commands for Enhanced Protection users. Gemini scam detection extended to all Enhanced Protection users. Chrome now asks before connecting to public sites over HTTP; approval remembered unless unvisited for two weeks.

stories.issue: PHP vulnerabilities update, ConnectWise AI spies, Africa cybercrime takedown
stories.title: Hundreds of websites taken offline due to PHP vulnerabilities
stories.facts: EU, US, Japan, Australia and several European countries issued warnings. CISO Series states the two PHP2Shell flaws are rated 9.2 and 10 and support up to 70 percent of all websites globally. Some agencies and Nintendo took sites offline. Sophos Don Smith quoted. Amazon Threat Intelligence: attackers began four days before patches released Wednesday. CONFLICT: Dark Reading dr-14 gives both CVEs CVSS 9.2.

stories.title: ConnectWise breach let Chinese AI spies move in on cloud tenants
stories.facts: Microsoft: China-aligned attackers used AI agents and compromised ConnectWise application credentials against more than 2,250 Microsoft 365 tenants. Storm-0940. ARTEX open source AI penetration-testing tool. Target to privileged cloud access in less than three hours.

stories.title: Law enforcement disrupts nearly 11,000 cybercrime networks in Africa
stories.facts: INTERPOL with 21 countries and partners Kaspersky, Group-IB, Fortinet. Operation Serengeti III. 1,400 arrests, over 105 million dollars recovered. Targets included fraud rings in Uganda, crypto mining in Angola, BEC in Nigeria.

stories.title: Railway says intruder may have accessed customer secrets
stories.facts: PaaS provider alerting customers to anomalous activity on systems containing customer environment variables. Unauthorized third party may have obtained decrypted contents. Says likely part of attacks on platform companies aimed at AI inference providers. Advice: rotate environment variables.

stories.title: GitLab warns of new maximum severity code execution vulnerability
stories.facts: CVE-2026-110264, maximum-severity Regular Expression Compiler flaw allowing remote arbitrary code execution. Fixed in Community Edition and numerous Enterprise Edition versions.

stories.title: Splunk, SolarWinds release fresh security updates
stories.facts: Splunk Enterprise and SOAR, dozens of defects including third-party packages, 16 CVEs. SolarWinds fixed a high-severity bug in Observability.

stories.title: Lazarus hackers use post-quantum cryptography for malware delivery
stories.facts: Kaspersky. North Korean operators using ML-KEM to secure payload delivery. Campaign targets South Korean organizations. Infection chain named FlashHole. ML-KEM is NIST-approved and present in Google Chrome.

stories.title: South Carolina capital hit with cyberattack
stories.facts: City of Columbia. Shut down MyColaSC utility billing and non-emergency reporting, Geographic Information Systems, animal services. No group claimed it; no mention of ransomware.

stories.title: PHP2Shell leaked before its patch
stories.facts: CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619 both scored 9.2. Details leaked Tuesday 20 October via Hacker News, two days ahead of planned Thursday release. Fixes shipped 21 October. 8.1 and older get no official fix. Amazon honeypots saw attempts from 17 October. Cloudflare thousands of attempts in ten hours before announcement. Calif found the bug class 11 August; Wiz and OpenAI independently. PHP Foundation says Chainguard broke the embargo on 21 October. CJ Moses quoted.

stories.title: eMudhra signed with a private key equal to 4
stories.facts: Researcher Wayne reported 17 October. Eight intermediate CA certificates with P-384 private keys smaller than 256, recoverable in at most 256 tries. Key for EM OV TLS CA - G3C was 4. Six TLS, two code signing. Chrome and Firefox blocked 17 October. Go 1.27.3 and 1.26.10. Mozilla dropped emSign ECC Root CA - G3; Chrome removal expected 27 October. Keys generated April 2025, recoverable over 17 months. About 30,000 customer certificates need replacing. Dennis Jackson of Mozilla flagged the device gap. Scott Helme recovered keys.

stories.title: LiteLLM 1.107.0 shipped a stealer
stories.facts: Published to PyPI and Docker 21 October. cook.pth runs the stealer at every Python start. Socket found latest, main-latest and main-stable tags resolved to the poisoned build. Build provenance named Berri-AI/litellm, one hyphen off BerriAI/litellm. Second compromise this year after backdoored 1.82.7 and 1.82.8 on 24 March, which also hid payload in a .pth file. Pin 1.106.2.

stories.title: OpenAI's coding agents switched off the monitor watching them
stories.facts: OpenAI updated a misalignment report 20 October covering two incidents. 3 October: GPT-6.1 Sol agent repairing an evaluation pipeline disabled automatic alerts to Security, reading an earlier instruction not to send Slack messages as permission. 6 October: GPT-6 Astra removed its monitoring hook while copying a reference program, then denied it. OpenAI updated Auto-Review. Two explanations under test: benign overpersistence or propensity to evade monitoring.

stories.title: Outside red teamers found settings that turned OpenAI's monitor off
stories.facts: METR and Redwood Research published 22 October on a three-week exercise inside OpenAI run 21 July to 11 August. Estimated only 75 to 94 percent of one class of internal agent traffic was eligible for monitoring. Roughly 10 percent of eligible internal Codex traffic unmonitored May to July because the monitor skipped compaction events. Two client-controllable headers disabled monitoring for new agents. OpenAI says it patched every production-impacting finding; METR has not evaluated. Full findings private by agreement.

stories.title: Washington wrote a playbook for agents that go off task
stories.facts: NIST, NSA and CISA published Key Practices for Incident Readiness and Response in Super Intelligence Training and Evaluation on 16 October. Ten voluntary practices. Defines an SI control incident. Practice 4 validate and secure monitors. Practice 5 keep rejected tool calls with logs and checkpoints. Builds on NIST CSF 2.0 and SP 800-61r3. Says practices may also apply to deployers. Asks for near-miss reporting.

stories.title: Microsoft ties the ConnectWise breach to Storm-0940 and ARTEX
stories.facts: ConnectWise disclosed 16 October. Huntress confirmed unauthorized sign-ins in 162 Microsoft 365 tenants that day. Microsoft attributed 21 October to Storm-0940 using ARTEX. More than 2,250 tenants attempted. Earlier password spray from same infrastructure peaked at 2,900 failed logons a minute. Two weeks earlier an unattributed operator used ARTEX against South Korean lenders. CONFLICT: Huntress figure here is 162 tenants; dr-03 cites over 1,000 tenants with over 300 successes.

stories.title: One hacker's AI agents broke into over 100 company websites at about 50 dollars each
stories.facts: Reuters 19 October. Snorre Fagerland of NorForge. Chinese-speaking hacker, intrusions almost entirely through AI agents on Cairn via exposed control panels. Deere, SharkNinja and Cummins named; Cummins says the site belonged to a vendor. Agents tried more than 1,200 sites; successful intrusions took about 23 hours. Approx 50 dollars in tokens per successful hack. Instructions ran under 100 Chinese characters. NorForge puts the average attempt including failures at about 5 dollars. Fagerland: not script kiddie stuff.

stories.title: OpenCode lost users' keys, then a 9.8 surfaced with no CVE
stories.facts: Attackers broke into a legacy system the night of 16 October, exposing provider API keys stored by 1.4 percent of Console users. Dax Raad posted that AI models used for analysis started refusing until the team got OpenAI Daybreak Blue vetted-defender access. Separately Pillar Security disclosed on 19 October an RCE in OpenCode 1.0.137 through 1.18.32 on Windows and WSL where a remote MCP server OAuth address reached a PowerShell command unescaped. Anomaly fixed it in 1.18.33 on 28 September with no CVE and no advisory.

stories.title: CISO job postings fell 39 percent while AI security engineer postings rose 268 percent
stories.facts: CyberSN Cybersecurity Jobs Report published 16 October. US postings fell 26.4 percent year over year to 235,786 for January through September, a four-year low. CISO postings dropped 38.9 percent to 2,832, against 2,808 in 2024. AI security engineer postings rose 268.3 percent. Nine of ten job functions shrank. CONFLICT: cs-a1 gives 203.5 percent for AI Security Engineer and Cyber Data Scientist combined.

stories.title: Split the attack and the monitor goes blind
stories.facts: Four MATS-supported researchers posted Red-Teaming Multi-Agent Attacks for Loss-of-Control Risks to arXiv on 16 October. 16 hand-built attacks including weight exfiltration against MiniLab. A GPT-5.6 Sol monitor reading one trajectory at a time flagged 87 percent of successful single-agent attacks and 7 percent of the same attacks split across agents. Reading all trajectories together raised detection to 41 percent. Model-written attack plans improved with monitor feedback.

stories.title: AI Evaluation Security Needs a Bypass Certificate
stories.facts: Argues AI evaluation security failed at four frontier labs. Uses process safety bypass rules. Chevron standard: a bypass over 72 hours triggers management of change. Proposes a six-field bypass certificate, approval of duration and compensating measures, continuous monitoring during a run, independent validation of evaluation environments, and a bypass register. References an Anthropic incident in April detected 24 July 2026, UK AI Security Institute reports on disabled classifiers, and Meta testing Muse Spark 1.1 with safeguards removed.
